name: Israel

facts.religion: Jewish about 73%, Muslim about 18%, Christian and Druze minorities

snapshot: Israel's 27 October 2026 election left no bloc with a majority, and President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, the first chance to form a government.
culture: Israel's culture mixes Jewish traditions from Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, Hebrew revived as a spoken language, and a large Arab minority. Shabbat shapes the week. Tel Aviv is a secular tech and nightlife hub, while Jerusalem holds sites sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims. Israeli TV dramas like "Fauda" and "Shtisel" have found global audiences.
society: Israel is a high-tech economy with mandatory military service for most Jewish citizens. Ultra-Orthodox exemption from the draft, judicial reform and the role of religion divide society. The 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, which killed about 1,200 people, and the war in Gaza that followed, which killed tens of thousands of Palestinians, transformed politics and Israel's standing in the world.
situation: On 7 October 2023, Hamas killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel, the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, on the watch of Benjamin Netanyahu, who had built his career as "Mr Security." What followed was a war in Gaza that killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and expanded to Lebanon, Syria, Yemen and in 2026 a direct war with Iran. Polls since 2023 have mostly predicted Netanyahu would lose the next election. On 27 October, Israelis finally get to vote.

It will be the first Israeli election held after a full four-year term since 1988. The opposition has consolidated: in April, former prime ministers Naftali Bennett, a right-wing former commando turned tech millionaire, and the centrist Yair Lapid merged their parties into a joint list called Together, led by Bennett (Al Jazeera). Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot leads another new party, Yashar. The pair united once before, in 2021, to end Netanyahu's 12 years in power, only for their coalition to collapse in 18 months. The race is tight. A Kan 11 poll in late September had Netanyahu ahead of Bennett 42 to 33 as preferred prime minister, while seat projections show Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc short of the 61 seats needed for a majority (Wikipedia polling table). Netanyahu, still on trial for corruption and seeking a pardon, has vowed to "do everything to win." The killing of Iran's supreme leader has given him a new security story to tell.
power: A parliamentary democracy with no written constitution. The prime minister needs a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat Knesset, elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3.25 percent threshold, so every government is a coalition; the president is ceremonial but chooses who gets the first chance to form one.
holders: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud), facing an election on 27 October.

update.html: Israelis voted on 27 October with turnout of 77.7 percent, the highest since 1999. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats, the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot 48 and Arab-led parties a record 19, so no bloc has the 61 needed. Parties with 67 seats recommended Eisenkot and parties with 46 recommended Netanyahu, and on 8 November President Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate, starting 28 days, to about 6 December, with a possible 14-day extension. The 26th Knesset is sworn in on 10 November. Eisenkot's bloc has nominated Matan Kahana of Yashar! to replace Likud's Amir Ohana as speaker, with the Joint List's backing, and Avigdor Liberman to chair the Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee; Ohana says he will hold a vote only if 61 MKs ask. Eisenkot wants a broad 'national emergency government', but Yisrael Beytenu and the ultra-Orthodox parties oppose relying on Arab parties, and United Torah Judaism demands a solution for yeshiva students. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new government is sworn in.
